title: Bidirectional A* on Seattle: Real Routing in ⚡
description: Watch how Bidirectional A* searches from both start and goal to meet in the middle—cutting work while keeping optimal routes. This is the same style of graph search concept routing AI uses under tight time constraints.
ig_caption:
Bidirectional A* on Real Maps: The Ultimate Pathfinding Algorithm — How autonomous vehicle routing AI finds the best route in milliseconds ⚡

In this Seattle (Capitol Hill) visualization, Bidirectional A* runs TWO informed searches at once: one forward from the start, one backward from the goal. As both frontiers expand using the same heuristic logic, they converge sooner—so fewer nodes get expanded than standard A*.

Mechanics (the “why it’s fast” part):
• Forward search prioritizes lowest estimated cost f = g + h from Start → …
• Backward search prioritizes lowest estimated cost from Goal → …
• When the two search waves touch (or the combined best path can’t be beaten), we reconstruct the optimal route.

Takeaway: Bidirectional A* is an optimization strategy for shortest paths on road-like graphs—often a big win when the heuristic is decent.

Debate question: Should “optimal route” mean minimum time, minimum distance, or minimum risk?
